messages:
Marta L: Quick sync: our ingest cost is spiking from a handful of high-cardinality attributes (model_variant, ff_id, user_segment). Proposal: compute an "attr_density" score per tenant+attr over a sliding 24h window and drive an automated compaction policy. Compact = store top-N + hashed exemplar + bucket fallback. Keep raw only for attrs above threshold or explicitly opted-in.

Kevin R: Sounds necessary. Two operational constraints: (1) billing & audit joins need canonical values. If we compact billing-affecting attrs we need a reversible mapping or persisted join table retained for billing window. (2) BI users will run adhoc group-bys; compaction will change result sets. We should add a warning header and a migration doc.

Priya S: Implementation idea: attr_density = unique_vals / rows_seen; threshold paramizable per-tenant (default 0.002). compact_policy: {top_k:50, exemplar_hash:sha256, buckets:[hot(0-95%), medium, other]} . Store policy metadata in the event envelope: `__attr_compaction:{attr:X, policy:v2, applied_at:ts}` so queries can detect compacted columns.

Jules: Queryability note: for time-series dashboards we need deterministic behavior. Suggest sticky-sampling 0.5% of events kept raw (for 7d) to enable distribution reconstruction and alerts on shift. Also add a reversible raw-archive stream (short-retention S3) before compaction to support on-demand replays.

Marta L: Ownership question 1: where should density be computed? Gateway vs ingest preprocessor? I prefer gateway+enrichment to allow private deployments to opt-in. But enrichment contract must be generic so other proxies can set the header.

Kevin R: Agree gateway-first. Add contract change: enrichment header `X-Attr-Compaction: {
